03 / INVENTORY
Inbound receiving and storage controls
Scan controls, variance rules and environmental limits.
3.1 Warehouse specialization
WRO-1 (Wroclaw) handles all chilled grocery stock and a limited ambient overflow zone. POZ-2 (Poznan)
handles the primary ambient catalog and returns inspection. A chilled order may be picked only at

WRO-1; POZ-2 does not hold chilled inventory.
3.2 Receiving and stock variance
Inbound pallets must receive their first dock scan within four hours of their recorded arrival. Each stock
keeping unit (SKU) is reconciled against its expected quantity. Escalate a variance to Inventory Control
when the absolute difference is greater than three units OR greater than 2% of expected quantity.
Exactly three missing units do not trigger the unit threshold, but can still trigger the percentage
threshold.

threshold.
For example, receiving 97 units against 100 expected creates a three-unit, 3% shortage and therefore
requires escalation. Receiving 197 against 200 expected creates a three-unit, 1.5% shortage and does
not cross either escalation threshold. Negative and positive variances follow the same rule.
3.3 Chilled conditions and sensor policies
The chilled-grocery storage target is 2-6 degrees Celsius. A temperature alert is raised when a monitored

location is above 6 degrees Celsius for more than 10 consecutive minutes. A quality hold is mandatory
when the measured temperature is above 8 degrees Celsius for more than 5 consecutive minutes. The
quality hold remains active until a documented release decision is recorded by the Quality Lead.
Stationary cold-room sensors are reviewed twice per operating day. Their formal calibration cycle is
annual, with the next documented calibration due on 15 January 2027. A missed calibration is a

quality-system finding and must be escalated even when temperature readings appear plausible.
THRESHOLD LOGIC
“More than” is strict. Exactly 10 minutes above 6 C is not sufficient for an alert; exactly 5 minutes above 8 C is
not sufficient for the mandatory hold.
